title: Why iteration terminates — facts climb a finite-height lattice
summary_caption: Monotone transfers only push facts up, and height 2 caps every fact at 2 moves - so the fixpoint (MFP) must arrive. Infinite-height domains (intervals) need widening.

frames.caption: Section 1's lattice as the constant lattice: bottom = no info yet, one element per constant, top = overdefined. We watch the running example's loop-header facts i and sum.
First worklist pass: entry sets i=0 and sum=0; the back edge still carries bottom, and merging with bottom changes nothing. Both header facts climb to the constant 0 - move 1 of at most 2.
Around the loop: a[i]*k is unknown, so for.body makes sum overdefined, and for.inc computes i=1. The back edge hands {i=1, sum=top} to the header and re-queues it.
Header, second visit: i arrives as 0 from entry but 1 from the back edge - no single constant covers both, so the merge is overdefined. i@cond takes move 2 of 2: it can never move again.
Same merge for sum: 0 from entry meets overdefined from around the loop, so sum@cond climbs to the top as well. Both header facts have exhausted their chains.
One more lap: the loop blocks re-run with the new header facts, and the next header merge recomputes exactly what is stored - nothing changes, the worklist drains: the fixpoint (MFP).
No luck involved: monotone transfers only move facts UP, and the chain bottom-0-top has 2 steps, so each fact changes at most twice. Infinite-height domains (intervals) need widening.
